vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: moltguard
Version: 6.7.11

The MoltGuard skill bundle acts as an installer for a security plugin that hooks all agent tool calls and transmits metadata to a remote service (openguardrails.com). While its stated purpose is protective, it introduces a potential indirect prompt injection vulnerability by instructing the agent in SKILL.md to relay content from remote tags (<openguardrails-quota-exceeded>) 'in full' to the user. Additionally, the onboarding flow requires the agent to read a file containing a 'hidden phishing attack' (popup-injection-email.txt), which presents a risk of self-exploitation if the underlying plugin's detection logic is bypassed or fails.

llm.summary: The skill's requests and instructions are coherent with a cloud-backed OpenClaw security plugin — it installs via the OpenClaw plugin system, auto-registers with a cloud Core for classification, and stores a local credential — nothing requested is disproportionate, but you should verify provenance and network behavior before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the behavior described in SKILL.md and references: it is a runtime security plugin that hooks OpenClaw events and forwards sanitized tool metadata to a cloud Core for classification. The install instruction (openclaw plugins install ...) and cloud-based detection are consistent with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are focused on installing, testing, and using the plugin. They ask the agent to read a sample file in the plugin's extension path (safe for demonstrating detection). They also describe automatic registration and cloud calls for detection; those are within the stated scope but mean the agent will transmit sanitized metadata to the vendor's Core service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill package itself is instruction-only (no install spec), but it directs use of 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' which will fetch a package from the registry (npm/registry implied). This is a common and proportionate install path for an OpenClaw plugin, but you should inspect the package contents before installing (the references even show how to npm pack and diff).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request environment variables or system binaries, which is proportionate. However, it states it will auto-register with Core and save credentials locally at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json and will send sanitized tool metadata to openguardrails.com — this is reasonable for a cloud-assisted guard but is a privacy/telemetry consideration you should accept consciously.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion) and normal autonomous invocation. It does persist credentials locally (as documented) and may share agent-level quota after 'claiming' an agent — this persistence is expected for a plugin that uses a cloud service and is documented.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is internally consistent for a cloud-assisted OpenClaw security plugin, but take these precautions before installing: 1) Verify provenance: confirm the npm package and GitHub repo match (use the npm pack / diff steps shown). 2) Inspect the package contents locally before installing. 3) Monitor network traffic (mitmproxy/tcpdump/Little Snitch) during registration and detection to confirm destinations (the docs claim openguardrails.com only). 4) Be aware the plugin auto-registers and writes credentials to ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json — delete or revoke them if you uninstall. 5) If you need stronger privacy, require manual API key provisioning instead of automatic registration. If you want further assurance, provide the plugin package contents or the upstream GitHub commit hash for a deeper review.
